title: Getting started with metacleaner
text: Reference databases DNA metabarcoding (example plant ITS2 databases built NCBI GenBank) contain sequences wrong name: fungal sequences submitted plants, sequences labeled wrong genus, sequences identical several genera identify . Reads match entries assigned wrong taxon. metacleaner checks every sequence database (query) three steps: match sequence database things (contaminants, e.g. fungal )? removed. match sequence database things (reference, e.g. plant )? , removed. reference sequences matches taxonomy query level choose (genus default)? belong different genus, several genera, removed. “match” means least identity percent identical least coverage percent query’s length. 100 default, identical sequences count. need programming experience software: everything, including sequence search, built package.

what: Automated curation of DNA barcode reference databases for metabarcoding and metagenomics
title: metacleaner: Automated Curation of DNA Barcode Reference Databases
text: DNA barcode reference databases built NCBI GenBank (example MetaCurator) contain mislabeled sequences. pollen metabarcoding plant ITS1/ITS2 databases, produces reads assigned fungi, wrong plant genus, several genera identity. metacleaner checks sequence database. removes sequence matches database unwanted sequences (e.g. fungal ), match database wanted sequences (e.g. plant ), matches wanted sequences whose taxonomy disagrees rank choose (genus default). Everything runs inside R. sequence search built (C++, multithreaded), need install BLAST, Python command-line tools.

what: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
text: Applies metacleaner decision rules search results. classification step used inside [clean_reference()]; call directly produced hit tables (example [search_sequences()]).

title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
code: classify_queries(   query_ids,   reference_hits,   contaminant_hits = NULL,   taxonomy,   level = "genus",   require = NULL,   rescue = TRUE,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
text: query_ids Character vector query IDs. reference_hits Data frame hits reference database, least columns `query`, `subject`, `identity`, `coverage`, `score` `pass` (returned [search_sequences()]). contaminant_hits Optional data frame hits contaminant database (columns), `NULL`. taxonomy find taxonomy; see [clean_reference()]. level Rank query hit taxonomy must agree. Default `"genus"`. require Optional named character vector length one, e.g. `c(class = "Magnoliopsida")`: every qualifying hit must belong taxon. rescue Keep queries without qualifying reference hit best hit agrees taxonomy `level` (see rule 2). Default `TRUE`, metacleaner 1.x. verbose Print progress messages.

title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
text: list elements `status` (one row per query: `id`, `flagged`,   `reason`, `database`, `top_hit`, `identity`, `coverage`, `n_hits`,   `hit_taxa`) `lineages` (lineage table used).

title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
text: query checked order; first rule applies gives reason flagged. 1. **matches contaminant database**: query qualifying hit (   `identity` `coverage`) contaminant database. 2. **match reference database**: query qualifying hit    reference database. `rescue = TRUE` query's best    non-qualifying hit belongs taxon query `level`,    query kept hit used checks . 3. **hit outside required <rank>**: (`require` set) least one    qualifying hit required taxon, taxonomy unknown. 4. **taxonomy query**: query's taxonomy `level`    unknown. 5. **matches multiple <level>**: qualifying hits belong one    taxon `level` (hit unknown taxonomy counts separate    taxon). 6. **matches different <level>**: qualifying hits belong one taxon    differs query's. Queries flagged rule kept.

title: Decide which query sequences to flag — classify_queries
code: hits <- data.frame(query = c("q1", "q2", "q2"), subject = c("r1", "r2", "r3"),                    identity = 100, coverage = 100, score = 1, pass = TRUE) tax <- data.frame(id = c("q1", "q2", "r1", "r2", "r3"), taxid = NA,                   domain = "Eukaryota", phylum = NA, class = NA, order = NA,                   family = NA, genus = c("Malus", "Malus", "Malus", "Malus", "Pyrus"),                   species = NA) res <- classify_queries(c("q1", "q2", "q3"), hits, taxonomy = tax, verbose = FALSE) res$status[, c("id", "flagged", "reason")] #>   id flagged                         reason #> 1 q1   FALSE                           <NA> #> 2 q2    TRUE         matches multiple genus #> 3 q3    TRUE no match in reference database

title: Clean a barcode reference database — clean_reference
text: query database clean: FASTA file path named character vector (see [read_fasta()]). Sequence names must accessions can found `taxonomy`. reference Sequences wanted group (e.g. plant sequences NCBI): FASTA file path named character vector. may contain query sequences . contaminants Optional sequences unwanted groups (e.g. fungal ): FASTA file path named character vector. `NULL` (default) skips step. taxonomy find taxonomy query reference sequences. One : * taxonomy file path (see [read_taxonomy()] formats), * `"ncbi"` look accessions online (see [taxonomy_from_ncbi()]), * path taxonomizr database ending `.sql`   (see [taxonomy_from_taxonomizr()]), * lineage table (data frame) returned [read_taxonomy()], * list / vector several , tried order: e.g.   `c("query.tax", "ncbi")` uses file first NCBI anything   file. identity Minimum percent identity hit (0-100). Default 100. coverage Minimum percent query covered hit (0-100). Default 100. level Taxonomic rank query hits must agree: one `"domain"`, `"phylum"`, `"class"`, `"order"`, `"family"`, `"genus"` (default) `"species"`. require Optional extra filter, e.g. `c(class = "Magnoliopsida")`: queries hit outside taxon flagged. (old command-line form `"class,Magnoliopsida"` also accepted.) rescue `TRUE` (default, metacleaner 1.x), query hit thresholds kept best lower-scoring hit belongs taxon `level`. Set `FALSE` stricter cleaning. exclude_self `TRUE`, query may match reference sequence accession. Default `FALSE`. engine Search engine: `"native"` (default, built ) `"blast"` (requires BLAST+; see [blast_available()]). threads Number CPU threads use, `"auto"` use available cores one. Default 1. search split across threads operating systems (including macOS); results identical whatever number threads. max_hits Maximum hits per query used taxonomy checks (best-scoring first). Default 100. outdir Optional output folder. given, results also written [write_results()]. prefix File name prefix output files. Defaults query file name without extension, `"metacleaner"`. verbose Print progress messages. Default `TRUE`.

title: Clean a barcode reference database — clean_reference
text: object class `metacleaner_result`: list   * `clean`: kept sequences (named character vector),   * `flagged`: data frame one row per removed sequence     reason, hit triggered taxonomies,   * `status`: one row per query sequence (kept ),   * `taxonomy`: lineage table kept sequences,   * `hits`: search results (`reference` `contaminants`),   * `settings`: settings used. Print summary; use [write_results()] save .

title: Clean a barcode reference database — clean_reference
text: 1. searches database unwanted sequences (`contaminants`, e.g.    fungal ) flags queries match one; 2. searches database wanted sequences (`reference`, e.g. plant )    flags queries without match; 3. compares taxonomy query taxonomy matches    chosen `level` (genus default) flags queries whose matches    belong different several taxa. match ("hit") counts reaches `identity` `coverage`. full decision rules listed [classify_queries()].

what: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
title: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
text: Reads FASTA file (plain text gzip-compressed, sequences one line wrapped many lines) named character vector. default sequence named accession, .e. first word header line, old-style NCBI headers `gi|12345|gb|AB123456.1|` reduced `AB123456.1`.

title: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
code: read_fasta(file, ids = c("accession", "header"), drop_version = FALSE)

title: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
text: file Path FASTA file. Files ending `.gz` decompressed automatically. ids sequences named: `"accession"` (default) uses accession (first word header); `"header"` keeps full header line. drop_version `TRUE`, remove version suffix accessions (`AB123456.1` becomes `AB123456`). Default `FALSE`.

title: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
text: named character vector: names sequence IDs values   sequences upper case.

title: Read sequences from a FASTA file — read_fasta
code: f <- system.file("extdata", "query.fasta", package = "metacleaner") seqs <- read_fasta(f) length(seqs) #> [1] 52 head(names(seqs)) #> [1] "MZ509216.1" "MZ509176.1" "MW545606.1" "MW545649.1" "MW545773.1" #> [6] "MW545611.1"

title: Read a taxonomy file — read_taxonomy
text: * **taxonomizr / MetaCurator input format** (also written   [write_results()]): comma-separated, header, columns `taxid`,   `accession`, `taxid`, domain, phylum, class, order, family, genus   species. Example:   `"49992","Z37472.1","49992","Eukaryota","Streptophyta",NA,"Lamiales",...` * **lineage strings** (QIIME, Metaxa2 similar): two tab-separated   columns, ID `;`-separated lineage, optionally rank prefixes   `k__`, `d__`, `p__`, `c__`, `o__`, `f__`, `g__`, `s__`. * **table header row** (tab- comma-separated) ID column   (`id`, `accession`, `seqid` `qseqid`) columns named ranks   (`superkingdom`/`kingdom`/`domain`, `phylum`, ..., `species`).

what: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
text: Finds, every query sequence, database sequences matches least `identity` percent identity least `coverage` percent query length (strands searched). search step used inside [clean_reference()]; users need call directly.

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
code: search_sequences(   query,   database,   identity = 100,   coverage = 100,   max_hits = 100,   best_hit = TRUE,   exclude_self = FALSE,   engine = c("native", "blast"),   threads = 1,   k = 12,   verbose = TRUE )

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
text: query Query sequences: FASTA file path named character vector. database Database sequences: FASTA file path named character vector. identity Minimum percent identity (0-100). Default 100. coverage Minimum percent query coverage (0-100). Default 100. max_hits Maximum number qualifying hits reported per query (best first). Default 100. best_hit `TRUE` (default), queries without qualifying hit also report best-scoring non-qualifying hit (`pass = FALSE`), one exists. exclude_self `TRUE`, query allowed match database sequence ID. Default `FALSE`. engine `"native"` (default) `"blast"`. threads Number CPU threads use, `"auto"` use available cores one. Default 1. search split across threads operating systems (including macOS); results identical whatever number threads. k Word length native engine index (8-13). Default 12. Smaller values sensitive low identity slower. verbose Print progress messages. Default `TRUE`.

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
text: data frame one row per reported hit columns `query`,   `subject` (database ID), `identity`, `coverage`, `score` (alignment score   native engine, bit score BLAST), `strand`, `qstart`, `qend`,   `sstart`, `send`, `pass` (whether hit meets thresholds)   `n_pass` (total number qualifying hits query, can   exceed `max_hits`).

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
text: default engine written C++ needs external software. database indexed k-mers (words length `k`). query q-gram filter computes many k-mers qualifying match must share query; database sequences pass filter aligned (banded local alignment megablast-like scores: match +1, mismatch -2, gap 2.5). filter derived thresholds, qualifying match missed thresholds high (identity 90 search exact containment test fast. Identity number identical positions divided alignment length (BLAST's `pident`). Upper/lower case U/T treated ; ambiguity code (e.g. `N`, `R`, `Y`) identical code. BLAST instead scores ambiguity codes mismatches, sequence containing can 100 engine BLAST. Coverage fraction query covered best alignment database sequence. BLAST's `qcovs` adds together several separate alignments sequence, coverage values close threshold can differ slightly engines.

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
text: `engine = "blast"`, BLAST+ (`makeblastdb` `blastn`, default megablast settings) must installed system `PATH`; see [blast_available()]. Identity `pident` best-scoring HSP coverage `qcovs`, metacleaner 1.x.

title: Search query sequences against a database of sequences — search_sequences
code: q <- c(q1 = "ACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGATCGATGCTAGCTAGG") db <- c(s1 = "TTTTACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGATCGATGCTAGCTAGGTTTT",         s2 = "ACGTACGTTAGCATGCATCGTTCGATGCTAGCTAGG") search_sequences(q, db, verbose = FALSE) #>   query subject identity coverage score strand qstart qend sstart send pass #> 1    q1      s1      100      100    72      +      1   36      5   40 TRUE #>   n_pass #> 1      1 search_sequences(q, db, identity = 95, coverage = 95, verbose = FALSE) #>   query subject  identity coverage score strand qstart qend sstart send pass #> 1    q1      s1 100.00000      100    72      +      1   36      5   40 TRUE #> 2    q1      s2  97.22222      100    66      +      1   36      1   36 TRUE #>   n_pass #> 1      2 #> 2      2

title: Save metacleaner results to files — write_results
text: * `<prefix>_clean.fasta`: kept sequences (one line per sequence); * `<prefix>_clean.tax`: taxonomy kept sequences; * `<prefix>_flagged.tsv`: one row per removed sequence taxonomy,   hit caused flagged, hit's taxonomy reason; * `<prefix>_summary.txt`: settings counts per reason.

title: Save metacleaner results to files — write_results
code: ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "metacleaner") res <- clean_reference(ex("query.fasta"), ex("reference.fasta"),                        ex("contaminants.fasta"), taxonomy = ex("taxonomy.tax"),                        verbose = FALSE) files <- write_results(res, outdir = tempdir(), prefix = "example") #> Results written to /tmp/RtmpX8yzUw: #>   example_clean.fasta #>   example_clean.tax #>   example_flagged.tsv #>   example_summary.txt files #>                                 fasta                              taxonomy  #> "/tmp/RtmpX8yzUw/example_clean.fasta"   "/tmp/RtmpX8yzUw/example_clean.tax"  #>                               flagged                               summary  #> "/tmp/RtmpX8yzUw/example_flagged.tsv" "/tmp/RtmpX8yzUw/example_summary.txt"

title: metacleaner 2.0.0
text: First release R package. complete rewrite Python/R command-line scripts (metacleaner.py + taxafilter.R) released v1.0.0 GitHub.

title: metacleaner 2.0.0
text: One function, clean_reference(), runs whole workflow; write_results() saves cleaned FASTA, taxonomy, report flagged sequences summary. Built-C++ search engine: BLAST+, Python, pyfasta shell tools longer required. Multithreaded platforms (threads, threads = "auto"). BLAST+ can still used engine = "blast". Taxonomy can come taxonomy file (taxonomizr/MetaCurator CSV, QIIME-style lineage strings table), NCBI web services (taxonomy = "ncbi", needed accessions looked ), local taxonomizr database, several turn. build_reference_db() download_ncbi_sequences() replace shell recipe building reference contaminant databases; read_fasta(), write_fasta(), dereplicate() extract_accession() replace awk/perl/sed/seqkit steps. FASTA files may wrapped gzip-compressed.

what: Bug fixes relative to the command-line version
title: metacleaner 2.0.0
text: Queries BLAST hit reference database never flagged; written clean FASTA missing clean taxonomy file. now flagged “match reference database”. BLAST output processed blocks 10,000 lines, query whose hits split across two blocks judged part hits. automatic taxonomizr database build never run. taxonomy step crashed sequence flagged. dot directory name broke search step. Flag reasons always said “genera”, whatever --filterlevel used. Database names used regular expressions split flagged list, similar database names (e.g. ITS_plant) confused. superkingdom rank longer exists current taxonomizr databases (now domain); handled transparently. pyfasta, required chunking, run Python 3.

title: metacleaner 2.0.0
text: flagged-sequence report one row per sequence (previously one row per hit) new columns database, identity, coverage, n_hits hit_taxa. max_hits = 100 qualifying hits per query used taxonomy checks (previously BLAST’s -max_target_seqs 10).
